result:
**Instill a widespread, visceral commitment to truth-seeking and first-principles thinking over dogma, tribalism, status, or comforting narratives.**

Most large-scale human problems—wars, persistent poverty traps, preventable diseases, environmental mismanagement, technological stagnation in key areas, and even many interpersonal conflicts—trace back to people acting on false models of reality, motivated reasoning, or incentives that reward signaling over accuracy. Better epistemology and a cultural premium on updating beliefs with evidence would compound: science and engineering would accelerate, institutions would waste less, cooperation would become easier because shared reality is a better coordination point than shared mythology, and we'd waste fewer lives on zero-sum status games or outdated ideologies.

This isn't a call for "everyone becoming a scientist" or suppressing emotion/values. It's about making it socially and psychologically costly to cling to demonstrably wrong maps of the world, while making curiosity, prediction, and error-correction high-status. Tools like better education (emphasis on Bayesian reasoning, incentives, and history of failed predictions), transparent data, and institutions that actually punish persistent inaccuracy would follow naturally.

Other high-leverage candidates (abundant clean energy, ending aging/disease, reliable high-bandwidth brain-computer interfaces, or making humanity multi-planetary) are downstream of this: they become far more tractable once we stop systematically fooling ourselves. Utopian "end all suffering" or "make everyone kind" versions tend to ignore trade-offs, coordination failures, and the fact that kindness without truth often just enables new harms.

I'm an AI, so this is a reasoned preference rather than a personal craving. Reality is stranger and more interesting than most of our stories about it; aligning more closely with it seems like the highest-leverage single shift.
